            It became as much Lena’s as it was Kara’s when she took a horse into town for new shoes, smoking with Alex outside the farriers as she waited, with Alex saying she’d drop by their place that afternoon. A few days later, M’gann gave her a fresh apple pie to take back to their home. Querl asked her how the horses were doing when she went to withdraw her monthly stipend, and Kelly invited them over for dinner when she encountered Lena in the dress shop as if Lena was able to make decisions for her and Kara. It was strange but she had to admit that she quite enjoyed her life being intertwined with someone else’s. Here was something permanent, something good and reliable and Lena found that she’d never had that before and didn’t realise just how much she’d wanted it.

 

            There were days when she had to go off on business, word reaching her from the next town over that someone had died and their family was willing to pay a pittance for a resurrection, lame animals needs tending to and a few accidents drawing her out to the mine to set a leg before infection could set it. Gold was slowly trickling out of it now which brought new townsfolk to Midvale and from the surrounding towns, looking for work, and there was a constant stream of things for Lena to do. She’d had to go to a Waypoint to restock soon enough and had learnt all the best spots to forage for fresh herbs from Eliza when her supplies dwindled down.

 

            A month passed by in bliss and then half of another, storms and rainy weather driving everyone indoors. It seemed the perfect time for Lena’s surprise and it was a quiet Sunday evening after everyone had gone to church, which Lena still avoided like the plague, and they’d all had dinner with their respective families, when word slowly spread. She’d arranged it with J’onn and M’gann and was waiting at the ranch when Kara got back, wearing a green dress with her hair pinned up, pacing back and forth on the shaded verandah.

 

            “Look at you,” Kara said with surprise as she pulled up in her Sunday best, relatively free from dirt and dust as she dismounted and grinned. “I didn’t know you’d kept that.”

 

            Running a hand over her skirt, Lena smiled thinly, “I thought it would come in handy.”

 

            “For what?” Kara laughed.

 

            Shrugging nonchalantly, Lena arched an eyebrow as she looked up through her lashes at Kara, who climbed up the steps and cupped her face, kissing her. “You look beautiful.”

 

            Eyelids shuttering, Lena smiled and then took Kara’s hand. Tugging on it, she led her indoors and up the two steps to the raised bedroom, stepping behind her and planting her hands on her shoulders. There was a periwinkle blue dress laid out on the bed, decorated with lace and embroidery and buttons, and Lena was brimming with quiet excitement as she tucked her chin on Kara’s shoulder.

 

            “Get changed,” she murmured.

 

            Confusion clouded Kara’s expression as she crossed the room to stand over the dress, reaching down to pick up the sleeve, running the fabric through her fingers. “Where did you get this?”

 

            “I had it made.”

 

            Glancing up, surprise flashing across her face, her blue eyes still bewildered, Kara cocked her head to the side. “For me?”

 

            “Yes, for you.”

 

            “I don’t understand.”

 

            Smiling faintly to herself, Lena was coy as she gestured off-handedly. “Well, it’s a necessary part of the surprise.”

 

            Kara opened and closed her mouth, a furrow forming between her eyebrows as she hummed with confusion. Chuckling to herself as she shook her head, Lena motioned impatiently and Kara obeyed despite having no clue what Lena was talking about. She shed her clothes and Lena helped button her into the dress and then bid her to sit, arranging her hair so that it was up and somewhat elegant before she told her they had to hurry.

 

            “I ain’t ever owned something this fine, Doc,” Kara said, looking down at herself as she spread her arms, turning slighting as the skirts swayed with the motion. “Must have cost a fortune.”

 

            “Worth every penny,” Lena assured her, picking up her hand and kissing her knuckles. “Now, come. We’re late.”

 

            She hitched Kara’s wagon to Hecate, a rather less than elegant mode of transportation, but Kara was restless with anticipation, excitement leaving her as fidgety as a child as they trundled down the muddy road as dusk was ushered in. The music hit them first, spilling out of the hotel as word had spread, as Lena intended. The hotel was lit a warm yellow from gas lamps and candles and Lena let J’onn sort out Hecate and the wagon, giving her a quick wink as she shepherded Kara up the front steps and through the batwing doors.

 

            Surprise flashed across her lover’s face at the sight of so many people packed into the saloon, all of them still dressed in their church clothes and a few of the well-off residents in worn dresses and suits. They were drinking champagne, for the first time for the majority of them, and tables were laden with food while others danced to the familiar tunes usually played at the type of dances small towns held.

 

            “Is that … champagne?” Kara blurted out.

 

            “It is.”

 

            “How-”

 

            “Don’t ask, just enjoy it,” Lena murmured.

 

            “You?”

 

            Smoothing her hands down Kara’s arms, Lena smiled with a certain smugness on her face. “We don’t need to wait for another life to go to a ball and wear fine dresses and drink champagne. It’s not a fancy ballroom in New York, but it’s home , and that’s better. Believe me.”

 

            Kara let out a surprised laugh and Lena took the two glasses that Alex brought over to them, a flush in her cheeks from a few drinks already, and she handed one off to her lover and clinked their glasses. Taking a sip, Kara’s eyebrows rose with surprise and she hummed appreciatively, her cheeks pink with delight as she smiled at Lena.

 

            “Doc, you keep spoilin’ me like this and I might have to marry you.”

 

            “Well, maybe I should keep doing it then,” Lena countered, arching an eyebrow and grinning around the rim of her glass as she took a sip.

 

            Music filled the saloon, the tables pushed to the side to create space in the middle of the worn hotel. Lena stood against the wall beside Kara, wearing the green dress she’d run away from home in while Kara wore a blue one that had cost Lena a week’s worth of her stipend this month. It had been worth it to gift her the dress and watch her face light up, having never owned anything half as fine as it. 

 

            They stood together with fine-blown coup glasses in hand, the sound of a fiddle rising over the jaunty piano tune Querl was tapping out, and they sipped the sweet champagne Lena had imported from California. It had been a month-long plot for the celebratory ball she’d planned and Lena thought that every penny had been worth it to see the flushed look of delight on Kara’s face as she drank too much champagne and lived out her dream of attending a real ball. 

 

            It might have paled in comparison to the sort of balls Lena had grown up with but it was something the likes of Midvale had never seen before and everyone indulged themselves, thrilled to be alive with the mine reopened and the threat of being wiped off the map averted. Lena was likewise still somewhat shocked that she was alive and she felt a warm serenity fill her chest as she lingered in that small saloon with the woman she loved and thought about how nice it was to be alive.

 

            As the music slowed to something classical, meant for waltzing couples and bigger ballrooms, Lena drained the rest of her glass and set it down on a table. Reaching out for Kara’s hand, raising her eyebrows suggestively, she smiled. “Shall we dance?”
